component.name: dsone
component.summary: Native Deezer and TIDAL client with bit-perfect audio

description.p: dsone is a native, lightweight desktop client for Deezer and TIDAL on Linux. It is a fork of SONE by Hassan Rabbi (lullabyX) that adds a native Deezer client next to the TIDAL one, while keeping SONE's audio engine: bit-perfect playback, exclusive ALSA output and full Signal Path transparency. Built with Tauri and Rust, it is small and fully native.

Deezer tracks stream in lossless FLAC (16-bit/44.1kHz) or MP3 depending on your subscription, and TIDAL tracks in lossless FLAC and Hi-Res up to 24-bit/192kHz, with gapless, silence-free playback. For bit-perfect output, exclusive ALSA mode bypasses PulseAudio and PipeWire entirely and sends the unaltered signal straight to your DAC; normal mode plays through PipeWire or PulseAudio for casual listening.

ul.li: Native Deezer client: library, playlists, search and lossless FLAC streaming
Native TIDAL client: lossless FLAC and Hi-Res streaming up to 24-bit/192kHz
Exclusive ALSA output that sends bit-perfect audio straight to your DAC
Bit-perfect mode with bit-depth promotion to your DAC's native depth
Automatic DAC format and sample-rate detection, with graceful fallback on mismatches
PipeWire and PulseAudio output in normal mode
Signal Path Transparency: inspect the live pipeline and confirm a bit-clean path to your DAC
Customizable light and dark themes, full-screen player and synced lyrics
Floating, resizable miniplayer and customizable keyboard shortcuts
MPRIS media controls, system tray and Discord Rich Presence
Scrobbling to Last.fm, Libre.fm and ListenBrainz
HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 proxy support

description.p: Unofficial client, not affiliated with Deezer or TIDAL. It requires an active subscription to the service you use, and is a streaming client only: it does not support offline downloads.

description.p: Deezer sign-in now happens in a dsone window; fixed Deezer and TIDAL links not reaching the app in the .deb, .rpm and Arch packages.
Deezer-first: TIDAL sign-in is optional, and Deezer sign-in opens Deezer's own page in the browser.
First dsone release, based on SONE 0.22.1

ul.li: New native Deezer client next to TIDAL
New application identity, with its own settings and cache folders
Flatpak bundle and native packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch Linux
